key_insight: Regional chemical potential (RCP) analysis reveals how bonding rearrangements guide selective Si adsorption on diamond (001), from single-dimer bridging to one-dimensional Si-chain growth and higher-coverage stripe/square-lattice phases.
engineering_relevance: The study offers a physically grounded way to predict and screen surface adsorption structures and electronic properties for Si-on-diamond surface engineering.
method: DFT calculations on reconstructed diamond (001) with Si adsorption
RCP real-space analysis to map electron-donating regions and bonding changes
Surface phase analysis and band-structure evaluation across increasing Si coverage
evidence_signal: The abstract reports computed adsorption energies, geometry optimizations, surface phase trends with effective Si chemical potential, and band structures showing gap reduction and Fermi-level crossings at high coverage.
watch_item: The conclusions are based on theoretical calculations, so experimental validation will be needed to confirm the predicted adsorption motifs and electronic phases.
paper_title: Application of Regional Chemical Potential Analysis to Si Adsorption on the Diamond (001) Surface
